podcast.title: Canadian Roots
podcast.body: A notable curiosity of Lost Wave songs is that a significant number of them appear to have roots in Canada, a phenomenon that has yet to be explained. "Now, you've probably noticed by now that for some reason a lot of Lost Wave songs have roots in Canada."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Defining Characteristics
podcast.body: Lost Wave refers to a category of songs that exist but are nameless, unclaimed, and missing from the musical record, often dubbed the "Jane and John Doe's of the music world." It is not considered a true genre because the songs don't need to share any sonic commonalities; their defining trait is simply being lost. "It's not really a genre because all these songs don't need to have anything sonically in common."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: The Challenge of Identification
podcast.body: Identifying Lost Wave songs has become a serious game for music fans, with significant prestige awarded to anyone who successfully cracks these "cold cases." This challenge is often referred to as "Challenge accepted." "However, much glory in a claim will go to anyone who correctly identifies any of them."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
